report.description: The warnings of the config that is now in force.

save_error.description: Why the write failed, as the system names it.

saved.description:
False when the config is in force and could not be written to the config file: a restart would come back with the config before. Sending the same document again tries the write again.
A write that was given up on after 10 seconds is not stopped, so the file may still come to hold this config. It never goes back to an older one.

Changes.description: Tags or names of one kind.

ConfigRefused.description: The data of a `config_refused` event: a reload or an apply that left the running config in force.

Control.description: What the control channel of the `veilway` inbounds did since start. Everything but `open` only grows.

accepted.description: TCP connections to the control port that the node took, and those that proved a transport secret of their device.

auth_failed.description: Connections closed for a wrong credential.

byes.description: `bye` messages written before a cut-off or a stop.

exits_selected.description: Exit selections that were taken, that were refused, and that a reload dropped.

malformed.description: Connections closed for a message that was malformed, not allowed where it came, or outside its bounds.

probe_runs.description: MTU probe runs that were started, probes from devices that were confirmed, probes the node sent, and datagrams to the probe port that were no probe of a live run.

replaced.description: Connections closed to make room for a newer one of the same device.

timed_out.description: Connections closed because the opening exchange was not done within 10 seconds.

handshake_age_secs.description: Seconds since the session the device has was made. Null without a session.

Diff.description: What an apply adds, changes and removes, by tag and name.

replay.description: `replay` changed. The rate per source is in force at once, the cache size from the next start of the node.

diff.description: Against the running config. Null for a document that is not valid.

Dns.description: What the node's resolver did with the DNS queries of its tunnels since start.

Document.description: A config version 1 document, see schema/config.v1.json. In an answer every secret (private_key, preshared_key, username, password, proxy_password) holds the marker "<redacted>", and every entry of transport_secrets holds a marker that names it, "<redacted:" with eight hex digits and ">". In a request a marker stands for the value the same object has in the running config: the inbound with that tag, the device with that public_key, the socks5 outbound with that tag and that server, the user with that name (proxy_password). A marker in transport_secrets stands for the secret of that device which it names, wherever it is in the list: an entry that is left out is removed, and a marker that names no secret of the device is an error. An outbound whose server is new or has changed needs its username and password written out.

ErrorBody.description: The one shape of every answer that is not a success.

interface_down_secs.description: Seconds since the interface went down. Null while `interface_up` is not false.

interface_flips.description: How often the interface switched between up and down.

interface_up.description: Whether the interface of an l3 backend is up. While it is not, what is routed to the exit is answered as unreachable and the node tries to bring the interface up again: 2 seconds after it went down, then after twice the wait each time, once a minute at most. Null for any other backend.

latency_ms.description: How long the proxy of the outbound took to answer the greeting of the last flow that dialled it, in milliseconds. Null for a direct outbound, for an exit with no SOCKS5 outbound, and until a flow has used the proxy. A reload starts it over.

link_up.description: Whether one of those links is up. While none is, what is routed to the exit is answered as unreachable and leaves no other way. Null for every other backend.

links.description: The node links of a chain backend, by tag, which `/v1/links` reports on. Empty for every other backend.

load.description: The `load` setting of the exit in the config. Null when the exit reports no load to apps.

load_level.description: The level apps are told: "low", "medium" or "high". Null while the exit has no `load` setting and until the node has looked twice, which it does every 10 seconds.

outbound.description: The tag of the outbound of a netstack backend.

udp.description: Whether the SOCKS5 proxy of the exit relays UDP as far as the node knows. Null for an exit without one.

udp_down_secs.description: Seconds since the proxy last refused to relay UDP. The node tries again once a minute. Null while `udp` is not false.

udp_flips.description: How often the proxy switched between relaying UDP and not.

ExitWorkingChanged.description: The data of an `exit_working_changed` event: the proxy of an exit stopped letting the node in (`working` false), or lets it in again. Devices without a choice of exit leave through another exit meanwhile.

details.description: For a config that was refused, every error with the path of its field. For a stale revision, one entry with the path `revision` and the revision that runs.

Host.description: an IP address or a lowercase host name, with no port

restart.description: The tunnel restarts and every session of it drops.

transports_started.description: Indexes into the transports of the new inbound.

transports_stopped.description: Indexes into the transports of the running inbound.

InboundInfo.description: An inbound with what a client profile takes from it. No private key.

public_key.description: The WireGuard public key of the inbound.

transport_public_key.description: The public half of the node transport key a profile carries. Null for an inbound with no `transport_keys`.

InboundTransport.description: One transport of an inbound, with the rating a profile of it gets.

public_addresses.description: The node's public addresses, as `GET /v1/status` gives them.

Key.description: a WireGuard key: 44 characters of standard base64 with padding

Lagged.description: The data of a `lagged` event: this many events, the ones whose ids are missing before the next event, never reached the reader. It was too slow for them, or the node made them faster than it keeps them for anybody. It has no id.

Link.description: One node link. It holds no key and no secret.

denied.description: On the exit half: why this node cut the link off. Null for a link that may run.

dropped.description: Packets that came out of the link and were not carried: on the entry half what answers no flow, on the exit half what the gate, the source check or a limit refused.

exit.description: On the entry half: the exit with a chain backend the link is behind.

flows.description: The flows the link carries: the translations of the entry half, or the flows of the exit half in the flow table.

handshake_secs.description: Seconds since the link's tunnel last completed a handshake. Null without a session.

size_warning.description: The system refused an outer packet of the link for its size within the last 600 seconds, which suggests the link's mtu is too high for the path. Anyone on the path can forge such a report, so it only warns.

state_secs.description: Seconds the link has been in `state`.

traffic.description: Inner packets. Up is what this node sent into the link, down what it took out of it.

transport.description: On the node that dials: the transport it is at, and the places of that transport and of its candidate or endpoint in the other node's list, from 0. Null on the node that is dialled.

oneOf.description: This node has the users and sends their packets into the link, through an exit with a chain backend.
What arrives from the link leaves from this node, under its own gate, rules and limits.

LinkId.description: the id of a link: 22 characters of base64url without padding

oneOf.description: The link connects to an inbound of this node.
This node dials the other one.
A WireGuard handshake completed within the last 180 seconds.
The node dials and has no session yet, or it is dialled and has heard no handshake yet.
The node dials and no candidate of the other node answers.
The node dials and the other node answers and does not take the proof.

No handshake for 24 hours, so the other node has ended the link or one of the two is misconfigured, or this node cut the link off for its quota or its expiry (`denied`). A node that dials tries once a day from here on.

Load.description: Apps show a user how busy an exit is in three coarse levels: below `busy` is low, from `busy` is medium, from `very_busy` is high. The node looks every 10 seconds and changes the level once the new one held for two looks in a row.

oneOf.description: Flows open on the exit, all users together.
Up and down traffic of the exit added together, in megabits per second, averaged over the last 30 seconds.

OutboundStats.description:
The counters of one outbound: those of the exits that leave through it, added up, with what the node knows of its proxy.
The node learns whether a proxy relays UDP once for each exit, from the flows of that exit, so two exits through one proxy can know different things for a while. This is what they know together.

down_reason.description: Why an `xray` outbound cannot carry a flow now, in words: the add-on is not installed or not running, Xray ended and starts again, or the name of its server does not resolve to an address the node may dial. Every exit through it is down with the same reason. Null while it carries, and for an outbound that is not `xray`.

latency_ms.description: How long the proxy took to answer the greeting of the last flow that dialled it, in milliseconds. Null for a direct outbound, and until a flow has used the proxy. A reload starts it over.

traffic.description: The sum of `traffic` over the exits whose backend names this outbound, all zero for an outbound no exit uses. It holds everything those exits count, which includes what their `unsupported` policy sent around the proxy with `"direct"`.

udp.description: Whether the SOCKS5 proxy relays UDP as far as the node knows: false while any exit through it was last refused. Null for an outbound that is no SOCKS5 proxy.

udp_down_secs.description: Seconds since the proxy last refused to relay UDP for any of its exits. Null while `udp` is not false.

udp_flips.description: How often the proxy switched between relaying UDP and not, added up over its exits. Exits that learn of one change each count it.

up_bytes_per_sec.description: The sums of the rates of those exits.

Problem.description: One problem of a config document: where it is and what was expected there. It never holds a value from the document.

ProxyStats.description: What one proxy inbound counted since it started. Everything but `open` only grows.

opened.description: Connections the inbound took, and those open right now.

refused_limit.description: Connections turned away at the inbound's `connections`, at a source's `per_source` and at `handshakes`, and logins refused unheard because a source had failed too many to that name.

refused_logins.description: Logins that were refused: no such user, a wrong password, a user the inbound does not admit.

refused_udp_source.description: UDP datagrams dropped because they did not come from the address and port the client named for its association, which is what a client behind a NAT that rewrites ports is refused for.

up_bytes.description: Bytes the clients sent to their destinations and got back.

Rated.description: The counters of one user, inbound or exit, with how fast they grew over the last seconds.

name.description: The user's name, or the tag of the inbound or exit.

Rating.description: What a censor can see of a profile's connection, computed here so that the panel and the clients agree. See PLAN.md, "three ratings".

Replay.description: The replay memory of the node. Times are Unix seconds on the node's clock.

disk_limit.description: The highest limit that may be on disk, which a start after a kill takes as its floor.

floor.description: A proof with a timestamp at or below the floor is refused.

floor_ahead.description: The floor is ahead of the clock in a way no start explains: more than 80 seconds, or risen while the node ran. Every proof of a client with a right clock is refused until the clock passes the floor or the replay memory is reset. After a start or a reset the floor is up to 80 seconds ahead, which is what they cost and is false here.

limit.description: A proof with a timestamp above the limit is not accepted before a higher limit is written.

limit_lowered.description: How often the node brought its own limit down after a clock that had run ahead.

ready.description: False while no proof is accepted at all: a reset whose file is not known to be on disk.

refused_floor_ahead.description: Proofs refused at the floor while `floor_ahead` was true.

refusing_secs.description: How many seconds the floor is ahead of the clock, whatever the cause: for that long proofs with a right clock are refused. 0 on a node that takes them.

writes.description: Writes of the replay file that went through, that failed, and that took more than 2 seconds.

more_errors.description: Errors beyond the first hundred, which are only counted.

shadow_cut_short.description: The check for rules covered by an earlier rule stopped at its budget.

ResetUsage.description: What a usage reset zeroes besides the quota count. The body may be left out altogether.

totals.description: Whether traffic, what the user sent and received in all, goes back to zero as well. Left out or false, only used_bytes and period_start start over.

SelfSigned.description: A certificate the node made for a `tls` listener, with the key it keeps.

listen.description: The listen address, as the config writes it.

not_after.description: Unix seconds, 80 to 100 days after `not_before`, drawn per certificate. Clients do not check it.

not_before.description: Unix seconds. The node makes the certificate anew with the same key 20 days before `not_after`.

pin.description: The SHA-256 of the key's SubjectPublicKeyInfo, in standard base64: the pin a profile's candidate carries with `self_signed`. It stays the same when the certificate is made anew.

Session.description: A device with a live session on one inbound. The address the device connects from is not part of it.

control_connections.description: The authenticated control connections the device has open.

flows.description: The flows of the device, through all its inbounds together.

mtu.description: The MTU the device set on the control channel. Null for a device that set none, whose tunnel has the `mtu` of its inbound.

selected_exit.description: The exit the device chose on the control channel for the action `"user"`. Null for a device that chose none and leaves through its user's exit.

transport.description: Null when the transport the device came over is gone.

drops.description: Packets that were not carried since start, by reason.

outbounds.description: Every outbound of the running config, in its order. An exit with an `l3` or `block` backend has no outbound and is in none of them.

proxies.description: Every proxy inbound (`socks5`, `http`, `mixed`) that runs, in the order of the config. An inbound that a reload changed starts counting over. Its bytes are in `inbounds` as well.

replay.description: The replay memory of the obfuscated transports. Null for a node that never ran one, which keeps no replay memory.

send_failed.description: Datagrams the node made for a device and no socket took, over every transport of every inbound. A socket of a `veilway` inbound never fragments, so a packet larger than the host's interface carries is counted here and not sent: lower the inbound's `mtu` when this grows.

state_write_failures.description: Writes of the usage state file that failed since start.

tunnels.description: Every tunnel that runs, in the order of the config. A tunnel that a reload changed starts counting over.

window_secs.description: The seconds the rates were taken over: 5 once the node has run that long, 0 before its second sample.

ws_stalled.description: WebSocket connections dropped because they never finished the upgrade, and refused at accept.

certificates.description: The self-signed certificates the node made for its `tls` transports with `"self_signed": true`, one for each listen address. Empty for a node that has none.

flows.description: Flows in the flow table right now.

generation.description: Starts at 1 and grows by one with every config that is put in force.

public_addresses.description: The node's public addresses, as the config names them: host names or IP addresses, with no port. A profile is given these, each with the port of one of its transports. Empty for a node that names none.

revision.description: What `If-Match` takes: 64 hex digits that name the bytes of the running config. Only this run of the node gives them this name: nobody else can work it out from a document, and after a restart the same config has another one.

Stream.description: What the stream listeners of the `tls` transports, and of the `ws` and `fronted` transports of `veilway` inbounds, did since start, and what they hold right now. Everything but `undecided`, `relayed`, `pending`, `sessions`, `proxies`, `decoys` and `fronted` only grows. Whoever is not a user gets the decoy origin's answer whatever the reason, and no reason holds an address, a path, a token or a key.

accepted.description: Connections the listeners took from the system, and failures to take one, which is what a host that is out of file descriptors shows.

broken.description: Connections that broke before they were decided, with an error that is no close: a reset inside the request line, or a connection whose own address could not be read.

ended_deadline.description: Sessions that ended, by reason: no WireGuard packet within 10 seconds of the proof, no chunk for 300 seconds, every chunk number used, the device's ninth session, a device or transport secret the config no longer has, a connection that closed or a peer that closed the session, a chunk that did not open or a frame the protocol does not allow, and a transport the config no longer has.

forwards.description: Requests handed to a decoy origin on the proxy path. `forwards_unframed` are those of them the node could not tell the end of, which it relayed to the end of the origin's answer and then closed the proxy's connection behind. `forwards_cut` are connections closed at once because one source had more than its share of requests waiting, or all strangers together more than half the proxy pool.

forwards_redialed.description: Requests that were sent to a decoy origin once more on a new connection, because the connection kept from the request before had been closed by the origin. `origin_dropped` are connections to a decoy origin that the node dropped between two requests because the origin said something or closed them there: nothing of that is passed on to the proxy.

handshake_failed.description: TLS handshakes that failed, that did not finish within 10 seconds, and that were closed to make room in the undecided pool.

handshakes.description: Inside sessions: handshake initiations above a session's allowance, datagrams WireGuard did not take as a packet of the session's device, datagrams for a device that were dropped because the send queue of its connection held 256, and chunks the node sent.

pending.description: Sessions whose proof was accepted and on which WireGuard has not authenticated yet, right now.

polls.description: `fronted` requests that were accepted, and repeats of the last accepted request that were answered with the stored response.

proofs_accepted.description: Proofs that were accepted, proofs that waited for the write of a higher limit, users whose request head was over a limit or no WebSocket upgrade, sessions that became established, and sessions that could not because the session pool had filled up since their proof.

proxies.description: The proxy path of the `ws` and `fronted` listeners, right now: connections of trusted proxies, requests on them that are in a decoy origin's hands or whose body is still read with nothing proven, and established `fronted` sessions.

proxy_accepted.description: Connections taken from a trusted proxy, and requests read on them. `proxy_unnamed` are those of them, on a listener with a `client_address_header`, in which that header named no source: the proxy itself stood for the visitor, so the limits per source were one limit for all of them. `proxy_idle` are connections closed after 300 seconds without a request.

proxy_http10.description: Requests of trusted proxies that were HTTP/1.0. None of them can be a user's: a web server that speaks HTTP/1.0 to the node shuts every user out, and has to be told to speak HTTP/1.1.

refused_limit.description: A timestamp above the written limit whose write did not end within 2 seconds or for which 64 other proofs waited already, and proofs that came while the node took none at all.

refused_pool.description: By a limit: the listener's session pool is full, the device has 2 pending sessions, or the device's or the source's allowance of accepted proofs is spent.

refused_window.description: Proofs of a device that were refused all the same, each of which took the decoy path too. By the replay rule: a timestamp outside the window of 60 seconds, at or below the floor, a token that was accepted before, and any while the cache is full.

relayed.description: Connections that are relayed to a decoy origin right now.

relays.description: Connections that were connected to a decoy origin and relayed, relayed connections that were closed to make room for another, and strangers that were closed with no answer because the origin could not be reached. While `decoy_down` grows the node can be told from its decoy.

shaped.description: `fronted-shaped` sessions that are established right now (`fronted` counts them as well), and event streams that are live right now.

shaped_polls.description: `fronted-shaped` requests that were accepted, repeats of one answered with its stored answer, repeats answered with the late answer of 80 bytes, event streams that were started, events and heartbeats written to them, and stream requests that their session's allowance of 4 at once and 1 a second had no room for.

stranger_head.description: Requests of the proxy path decided "not a user" for a reason only that path has: a head above 16,384 bytes or not complete within 10 seconds, a `fronted` request that names a session with a number out of order or while another request of it is in flight, one whose body was late, did not open or was a repeat with other bytes, and an opening request whose session no WireGuard packet established.

stranger_syntax.description: Connections decided "not a user", by the class of the reason: a byte that cannot be part of a user's request line or a line above 4,096 bytes, `stranger_syntax`. A line that was not complete within 10 seconds, `stranger_slow`. A peer that closed its side first, `stranger_closed`. A connection decided at once to make room in the undecided pool, `stranger_displaced`. A connection whose decoy origin said something or closed while the request line was not complete, `stranger_origin`. A complete request line that is no proof of a device, `stranger_proof`, which is where a wrong path, a wrong token and a removed device are counted alike.

undecided.description: Connections that have not been decided yet, right now: inside their TLS handshake or their request line.

upgrade_learned.description: How often the header fields of the upgrade answer were learnt from a decoy origin, and how often that failed. While the last try failed, the upgrade answer carries only `Date` of `upgrade_headers`.

Traffic.description: Inner IP packets and their bytes since the node first knew the name. Up is from the device into the node.

Transport.description: The transport a device came over, as the config names it: `ws` is the relay of a `wireguard` inbound, and on a `veilway` inbound the native WebSocket session behind the operator's web server.

TunnelStats.description: What one tunnel counted since it started. Everything but `open` only grows.

connect_failed.description: TCP connections the far side did not open within 10 seconds or refused.

dropped.description: Packets from the link that a full queue or an unknown session could not take, and datagrams that did not fit the link.

opened.description: TCP connections or UDP sessions the tunnel took, and those open right now.

refused_sources.description: Connections refused (TCP) and datagrams dropped (UDP): from an address in none of `sources`, past `max_connections`, past the 16 of one source, past 8 new ones a second for one source, while the `chain` exit was down, and for want of a translated port.

reset.description: TCP connections that a reset or the link going down ended, and those closed after an hour with no byte.

up_bytes.description: Bytes of the clients' own data towards the far side (up) and back (down).

up_packets.description: Inner IP packets sent into the link and taken out of it for the tunnel.

UdpObfs.description: What the `udp-obfs` transports did since start, and what they hold right now. Everything but `pending`, `sessions` and `tags` only grows. A datagram that is dropped gets no answer whatever the reason, and no reason holds an address, a tag or a key.

ended_deadline.description: Sessions that ended, by reason: no WireGuard packet within 10 seconds of the opening packet, no activity for 180 seconds, 2^31 packets sent, a newer session of the same source and device, the device's ninth session, and a device or transport secret the config no longer has.

handshakes.description: Handshake initiations above a session's allowance, datagrams inside a session that WireGuard did not take as a packet of the session's device, and packets the node could not make.

limit.description: Opening packets with a timestamp above the written limit that were dropped: the listener already kept 64 others, or no write ended within 2 seconds. And those that came while the node took no proof at all.

opened.description: Opening packets that were accepted, and sessions that became established.

pending.description: Sessions whose opening packet was accepted and on which WireGuard has not authenticated yet, right now.

sent.description: Packets the listeners made for a socket. Every one is a data packet of an established session, so a node that only strangers talk to has 0 here.

sessions.description: Established sessions right now, with those that a newer session of the same source replaced and that are still readable for 10 seconds.

short.description: Datagrams dropped, by reason: shorter than a data packet, `short`. No data packet of a session at its source and a tag that is not in the tag table, `unknown`, which is where every datagram of a stranger is counted. A tag that is in the table on a packet that does not open, `open_failed`: its sender holds a tag of this epoch without the device's secret, or the packet was changed on its way.

source_devices.description: Opening packets refused by a limit: the source has sessions of 4 other devices, the listener's session pool is full, the device has 2 pending sessions, or the device's or the source's allowance of accepted proofs is spent.

table_rebuilds.description: How often a tag table was built for a new epoch, how often that was late, how often a build did not end, and tags that were left out because another secret had the same.

tags.description: Epoch tags in the tag tables right now: three for each transport secret of each device that may connect.

waited.description: Opening packets that were kept for the write of a higher limit and taken to the replay rule again when it had ended, and opening packets a limit refused whose salt was recorded as spent, so that nobody who saw one can use it later.

window.description: Opening packets of a device that the replay rule refused: a timestamp outside the window of 60 seconds, at or below the floor, a packet that was accepted before, and any while the cache is full.

Upstream.description: What the node is doing for one upstream. Nothing in it is a key, a secret, a token or the link.

exit.description: The exit of the provider in use, and the exits it offers.

expires_at.description: When the document stops being current and when it was last refreshed, in Unix seconds.

mtu.description: The largest packet the carrier takes now. Null until a profile is in use.

notices.description: What the provider says to the device, as plain text.

pending_move.description: A move of the provider's endpoint, and refresh hosts, that the provider announced and the operator has not confirmed. The old endpoint and hosts are used meanwhile.

profile.description: The profile in use, and the transport it is connected over.

reason.description: Plain words for why the state is what it is. Empty while it is up.

refresh_error.description: Why the last refresh failed. Null once one has gone through.

signing_key.description: The fingerprint of the signing key the document in force is signed under. After the provider rotated its key this is the new one, which `signing_key` and the link in the upstream's config do not name until the operator confirms it.

state_secs.description: Seconds the upstream has been in `state`.

UpstreamClass.description: A class of transports the operator allows an upstream to use, as the client engine ranks them from strongest to weakest. `cover` is always allowed.

oneOf.description: `tls`, `ws`, `fronted` and `faketls`: they look like web traffic.
`udp-obfs`: no cover, but not recognizable by its bytes.
`ws-plain`: a WebSocket on plain HTTP, whose handshake can be seen.

UpstreamConfirm.description: What the operator confirms: the move of the provider's endpoint the node reported as pending, and the refresh hosts it reported. A field that is left out is false when the other one is given, and the body may be left out altogether, which confirms both.

hosts.description: Take the new refresh hosts and static mirrors the provider announced.

move.description: Follow the move to the new endpoint: the next refresh tries it first.

UpstreamConfirmed.description: What a confirmation did: false for each thing that did not wait for it.

UpstreamCounters.description: Totals since the node started, or since the upstream first ran.

dropped.description: Packets out of the tunnel that answered no live flow of a device, and were dropped.

refused.description: Flows refused because the upstream was down.

sent.description: Packets handed to the provider's tunnel, and packets it had no room or no session for.

state_flips.description: Changes between up and not up, and starts of the tunnel over again.

UpstreamDeclined.description: What a decline of a preview did: the provider was told to release the place.

UpstreamPreview.description: The answer to a preview: the document the provider sent, verified under the key of the link, as the operator reads it before saying yes. Fetching it took a place at the provider. The place is given back when the preview is declined or runs out, and made permanent by the config that names the same link and device within `expires_in_secs`.

account_expires_at.description: When the account ends, in Unix seconds. Null for never or unknown.

classes.description: The classes of transports the profiles list: the operator's consent is asked for each besides `cover`.

device_limit.description: How many devices the account may have, null for no limit or unknown, and how many the document lists.

expires_at.description: When the document stops being current, in Unix seconds.

expires_in_secs.description: How long the node keeps the document for the config that names it.

fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of the key the document is signed with, which is the one in the link and the one for `signing_key` of the config.

provider.description: The provider's own name for itself, shown as its claim next to the fingerprint.

UpstreamPreviewRequest.description: What the node needs to fetch the subscription of another provider with a device the panel made. The key and the secret are used for the fetch and are never in any answer, log or error.

allow_private.description: Whether the node is to be allowed to dial private addresses of the profiles. It decides which profiles the review marks as refused.

device_secret.description: The device secret, 16 bytes as 22 characters of base64url.

link.description: A native veilway://sub/ link. Carried, file, legacy and plain-address forms are refused.

private_key.description: The WireGuard private key of the device, 44 characters of standard base64 as a config writes a key.

via.description: The tag of a direct or socks5 outbound of the running config the provider is reached through. Left out: from the node itself.

UpstreamProfile.description: One profile of a provider's document.

exits.description: The exits the provider lists for the profile, by tag and name.

private_addresses.description: Private addresses the profile names to dial.

rating.description: What a censor can see, worked out by the node.

refused.description: Why this node would not use the profile under the request's settings. Null when it would.

UpstreamQuota.description: What the provider says an account has used and has. A quota of 0 is none.

UpstreamRemoved.description: What a removal did. `confirmed` says whether the provider took the word that the device left; when it did not, the place stays until the provider removes it. The upstream is not run again by a config that still names it.

UpstreamRetried.description: The tag of an upstream the node was asked to connect again.

UsageReset.description: The data of a `usage_reset` event: the user's quota count was started over through the API, and with `totals` their traffic counters went back to zero as well. A user who was out of quota gets a `user_restored` right behind it.

denied.description: Why the user cannot connect right now. Null for a user who can.

dns_set.description: The tag of the DNS set that names the user, or else one of their groups. Null when no set does: the user's queries then go to the set that names the inbound they come through, or to `dns.servers`.

period_start.description: When the count last started over, in Unix seconds. 0 for a user who never had a `quota_period`, or who had none when their usage was last reset.

used_bytes.description: Bytes in both directions since `period_start`, which is what `quota_bytes` is held against.

UserChange.description: Devices are named by their public key.

devices_secrets_changed.description: Kept devices whose transport secrets changed.

lost_access.description: The user could connect and no longer can.

installed.description: Whether the add-on's executable is in the add-on folder.

release.description: The release of Xray-core this node runs.

info.description: HTTP/1.1 and JSON on the unix socket of a node. Whoever can open the socket is the administrator: there is no other authentication. Every answer that is not a success has the shape of ErrorBody. No answer and no event holds a secret.

500.description: replay_unwritten: the replay file could not be written, so the reset may or may not be on disk. The node accepts no proof until it has written the floor and the limit it had back, and the reset has to be asked for again. replay_writing: the write has not ended within 10 seconds and the reset is in force when it does, so it must not be asked for again: replay.resets of GET /v1/stats grows by one when it has landed.

post.summary: Resets the replay memory of the obfuscated transports: the cache of accepted proofs is emptied, and the floor and the limit become the node's clock plus 60 seconds, written to the replay file before the next proof is accepted. It ends the state in which the floor is ahead of the clock. It costs two things: every client is refused for 60 seconds, and a proof that was accepted with a timestamp above the new floor is forgotten, so whoever recorded it can use it once more when the clock reaches that timestamp. Nothing else of the node is touched, usage and quotas included. The answer is the replay memory after the reset.

post.summary: Fetches the subscription of another provider from this node, with the device the body gives, and shows what the document holds. The fetch is the enrollment: it takes a place at the provider, so the provider sees this node's address and never the panel's. The document is verified under the key in the link, kept in memory for ten minutes under the id, and nothing is written to the config or the state file. A config that names the same link and device within that time takes the document and makes the place permanent without asking the provider again. At most four previews wait. The private key and the device secret are never in an answer.

delete.summary: Removes an upstream: the provider is told that the device left, for at most ten seconds, and the document and the keys leave the state file. The answer says whether the provider took the word. When it did not, the document stays in the state file and the same call again tells the provider again; the answer is 404 only when the running config has no such upstream, so a removal that was not confirmed can be retried while the config still names it. The upstream stops, and a config that still names it does not start it again, not even after a restart (a tombstone in the state file keeps it down until a config that no longer names it that way has been in force); apply a config without it to finish. A config applied without the upstream, with no call to this route, never tells the provider anything.

post.summary: Starts a user's quota count over: used_bytes is 0 and period_start is the start of the quota period the node's clock is in, or 0 for a user without a quota_period. A user who was out of quota may connect again at once, with no reload. traffic stays as it is unless the body says {"totals": true}, and the body may be left out. The state file is written before the answer. The same request again changes nothing more. The answer is the user as GET /v1/users/{name} gives them.
